definitions.explanation: A casual conjunction used to contrast or introduce an exception. Used at the beginning of sentences.
When attached to nouns, means 'even' (e.g., {子供|こども}でも - even a child).

examples.japanese: ⟦{行|い}きたい→行く：00119_iku⟧。でも、⟦{時間|じかん}→時間：00468_jikan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧。
examples.english: I want to go. But I don't have time.

examples.japanese: でも、⟦それ→それ：00994_sore⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{本当|ほんとう}→本当：00779_hontou⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。
⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。でも、⟦おいしい→美味しい：00740_oishii⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
⟦{疲|つか}れました→疲れる：00901_tsukareru⟧。でも、⟦{楽|たの}しかった→楽しい：00817_tanoshii⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
examples.english: I'm tired. But it was fun.

examples.english: That shop is a bit far. But the food is very delicious, so I often go there on weekends.

notes:
でも covers two distinct jobs that happen to share a shape: a sentence-initial conjunction (sense 1) and a particle attached to a noun (sense 2). Learners meet the conjunction first, but the particle is the more productive of the two.

AS A CONJUNCTION (sense 1):
でも starts a new sentence and pushes back against what was just said. It is the everyday spoken choice — softer and far more conversational than ⟦しかし→しかし：00986_shikashi⟧.
- Position: sentence-initial only. Never use it to join two clauses inside one sentence; that job belongs to ⟦けど→けど：09477_kedo⟧ or ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧, which attach to the end of the first clause.
- ⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧⟦けど→けど：09477_kedo⟧、⟦おいしい→美味しい：00740_oishii⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧ and ⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。でも、⟦おいしい→美味しい：00740_oishii⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧ say the same thing; only the packaging differs.

AS A PARTICLE (sense 2):
Attached directly to a noun, 〜でも picks out something as an extreme or unremarkable case, and lets the rest of the set follow by implication.
- "Even": ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧でも⟦{分|わ}かる→分かる：00463_wakaru⟧ — if even a child understands, so does everyone else.
- "Or something": ⟦お{茶|ちゃ}→お茶：00576_ocha⟧でも⟦{飲|の}みませんか→飲む：00322_nomu⟧ softens an invitation by presenting tea as one casual option rather than a fixed demand. This is the standard polite way to propose an activity.

WITH QUESTION WORDS:
Attached to an interrogative, 〜でも produces a free-choice "any-" word. These are common enough to have their own entries:
- ⟦{何|なに}→何：00498_nani⟧ → ⟦{何|なん}でも→何でも：00304_nandemo⟧ (anything)
- ⟦{誰|だれ}→誰：00534_dare⟧ → ⟦{誰|だれ}でも→誰でも：08498_daredemo⟧ (anyone)
- ⟦いつ→いつ：00536_itsu⟧ → ⟦いつでも→いつでも：03826_itsudemo⟧ (anytime)
- ⟦どこ→どこ：00539_doko⟧ → ⟦どこでも→どこでも：08499_dokodemo⟧ (anywhere)
Note the reading shift: {何|なに} becomes {何|なん} before でも.

REGISTER:
でも is informal. In writing, presentations, and business email, use ⟦しかし→しかし：00986_shikashi⟧ or ⟦ところが→ところが：00406_tokoroga⟧ instead. The particle 〜でも carries no such restriction and is at home at any level of politeness.
